components.css: .ds-assistant { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; min-height: 360px; padding: 12px; border: 1px solid #1b3547; border-radius: 12px; background: #071522; color: #e3f0f3; font: 400 12px/1.55 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; } .ds-message { flex: 1; padding: 12px; border: 1px solid #2c6175; border-radius: 9px; background: #0b2332; } .ds-message p { margin: 6px 0 0; } .ds-author, .ds-composer label { color: #6de5ed; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: .08em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-composer { display: grid; gap: 7px; } .ds-composer textarea { min-height: 64px; border: 1px solid #294a5f; border-radius: 7px; padding: 9px; background: #061521; color: #e8f2f5; } .ds-composer button { justify-self: end; border: 1px solid #47dbe9; border-radius: 9px; padding: 8px 12px; background: #47dbe9; color: #03121a; font-weight: 700; } .ds-composer button:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #2457d6; outline-offset: 3px; }

narrative.overview: Atlas Travel frames travel planning as a calm, high-confidence operations surface. Near-black space, local satellite geography, and restrained cyan trajectory lines make the physical route tangible without presenting a real booking system. The visual drama belongs to the interactive Earth. In AI Assistant mode, the route context stays compact at left, the globe remains visually open, and a persistent right-side conversation rail owns the full available workspace height.
keyCharacteristics: A real-geography 3D globe is the primary workspace object.
Cyan signals active spatial context; amber marks route endpoints.
Dense but quiet panels support, rather than compete with, the globe.

rules.name: The Sparse Signal Rule
rules.body: Cyan is an operational signal, not a decorative fill; reserve it for the route, interactive controls, and essential status.

rules.name: The Task-First Rule
rules.body: The globe introduces the trip; the current decision owns the largest usable area. Never make a dense decision flow compete with the globe or sit below redundant route context.

dos: Do keep geographic rendering real while explicitly labeling routes and planning content as illustrative.
Do keep the assisted chat header and composer reachable while its feed scrolls internally.
Do use cyan and amber with intention, preserving contrast on dark surfaces.
donts: Don't imply bookings, suppliers, map traffic, or travel data are real.
Don't turn supporting panels into bright competing focal points.
Don't make motion required to understand or operate the assisted workspace.
